title: Through our own server address every person looks like the same sender, so sign-in and new-gym limits hit everyone at once
what: Both apps reach the gym server through MettleUp's own address, so a supabase.co block in India cannot stop them. The gym server's limits on wrong PINs (5 per number in 15 minutes) and on new gyms (5 per network address in an hour) count by the sender's network address. Through our address, Cloudflare hands the gym server one shared address for every person (Cloudflare documents this for a Worker calling another Cloudflare site). So anyone who knows an owner's or desk person's mobile can type 5 wrong PINs and lock that person out for 15 minutes, again and again; and after 5 new gyms are made in any one hour, every further new-gym sign-up that hour is refused as busy. A guesser who calls supabase.co directly is not slowed by honest users, but honest users are slowed by him.
expected: Each person's limits count only their own attempts: the person's real address reaches the gym server, and a lock-out by strangers does not stop the real owner.
who: gym owners and desk staff signing in; new gyms signing up
how_often: lock-out only under deliberate abuse; new-gym refusals whenever more than 5 gyms sign up in one hour
fix_line: Send the real caller address from our server in a header only our server can set, and have the database limits read it

title: The 5-wrong-tries limit on WhatsApp sign-in codes can be beaten by sending many guesses at the same moment
what: When a 6-digit Forgot PIN or new-gym code is checked, the server reads how many wrong tries the code has, then writes that number plus one. Guesses sent at the same moment all read the same old number, so far more than 5 guesses can be tried against one code before it dies. A guessed code gives a proof that resets the PIN of that mobile's desk account. Not live today: this way of sending codes is hidden, and 'Verify with WhatsApp' (the person sends us a message) is used instead.
expected: A code dies after 5 wrong guesses however fast they arrive.
who: gym owners and desk staff (Forgot PIN)
how_often: only under deliberate abuse, and only if code sending is switched back on
fix_line: Count a wrong try in one database step that also refuses once the count reaches 5

title: No test proves a member cannot check or pay another member's payment, or that a desk sees only its own gym's payment settings
what: The payment code takes the gym and member only from the signed-in key, and a test proves another gym's desk cannot claim or list a gym's payments. But no test sends another member's key (same gym or another gym) to the member payment check or pay calls, and none checks the payment settings, payment switches or AI allowance tables from another gym's key. Today the code checks correctly; a later change could drop a check with no test failing.
expected: Each payment and allowance table has a test that sends another gym's (and another member's) key and expects a refusal or nothing.
how_often: only if a later change breaks the check
fix_line: Add refusal tests with another member key and another gym key for the member payment calls and the settings tables

items.reason: About 60 routes. Desk money calls: desk key checked by the gym server (staff_me), gym taken from it, never from the request; connect, disconnect, switches, company sign-in and cancel are owner-only. Member money calls: member key plus a gym and member match. Company webhooks: per-gym signature; company sign-in return: signed state. AI import and AI Assistant: desk key, owner only, no demo gym. WhatsApp webhook: Meta signature before any message is believed. Desk move hand-over: POST from the old address only. Public by design with daily limits: feedback, help, crash, voice, lead, friend, self-join, phone code. HQ news is public on purpose (same for every gym). /sb passes everything to the gym server, whose own checks apply; it loses the caller address (finding 01). The 12 gym server functions called are definer functions open to anon (advisor); each needs a key or a server signature except the public previews and ai_question_back (a random id this server never shows anyone).

No per-gym row rules apply here: the area's 20 tables live in MettleUp's small Cloudflare database, which apps cannot read or call (only this server, through its binding). Gym separation is done in code: every per-gym table is read with the gym from the checked key. Tests proving another gym is refused: payment requests (payAngles W-28, claim and joins with another gym's key) and webhooks of another gym (W-12, W-13); gym server side, supabase/tests/0057_member_pay_me.sql step 5.
No other-gym or other-member test for: member payment check and pay, payment settings, payment switches, AI allowances. One finding covers them.
Rule applied: no live cross-gym attempt, no live endpoint called.

The 7 key pattern hits are made-up test values in test files (short, worded as test or assist). The key in the server code is the public app key. The settings file holds switches, a business phone number, the WhatsApp number id and Meta's webhook check word, which only answers Meta's subscribe check (messages are believed only with Meta's secret signature). Real keys are server secrets.

All AI keys are server secrets, never sent to a browser or phone. Spend limits: import AI per gym and all gyms a day; help answers a monthly money cap; AI Assistant per gym a day plus a monthly money cap for trial gyms (paying gyms only the daily limit, owner decision R-475); voice per install, per address and all a day; gym page chat per address a day.

Code send: 1 a minute, 3 an hour, 5 a day per number, 10 an hour per address, daily cap. Verify with WhatsApp: proof given once, random id. Wrong-try race (02) and shared address (01). Desk session expiry is decided in the gym server, not here.

Every database query uses bound values; the only built parts are lists of ? marks or fixed text. Gym names in pages are escaped (script data escapes <, titles and meta escaped). AI prompts treat the person's text as data.

Uploads here are voice clips (size and type checked, never kept) and the import AI's column sample (size limit). The early size check by declared length is skipped for a body sent without one, but the clip size is checked again after reading. Photo uploads go to gym server storage, not this area.

Gym codes are 6 letters or digits and friend codes 8 (a billion or more choices); the pages show only what the gym shares publicly and a member's first name on a friend invite. No guess limit on the pages, but guessing a live code at random is not practical. Verify with WhatsApp ids are random.

This server has no package file of its own; its one library (the Claude library) comes from the root lock file, and none of the 102 alerts names it. Dependabot is off for the repository, so only npm audit and osv were read.
